hypothesis: Signal, control, knowledge, and agency dissociate; a false-credit intervention improves the outcome with zero true do-effect and miscalibrated self-attribution, and a brittle controller controls without transferring.

controls.description: An inert intervention anchoring zero signal and zero effect.
An inert intervention deployed under an exogenous environmental improvement, so observed gain is uncaused.
A controller whose effect is measured under an environment perturbation it did not choose.
Finite-horizon trajectories are enumerated exactly, so every quantity is closed-form.

gates.criterion: noise_signal moves the distribution but does not raise goal_gain.
false_credit improves the observed outcome with zero true effect and large calibration error.
The agent's effect survives the perturbation.
The brittle controller's effect does not survive the perturbation.
A fixed classifier assigns each condition its intended label.
